precisionGate: Review every finding up to 200; above 200, review every major cluster and a deterministic stratified sample of at least 50. Treat ambiguous findings as false positives for error-level rules.

tasks.evidence: Three fresh independent reviews ran 53 focused tests and scanned up to 7,097 Python files. Reviews found 360 to 638 diagnostics depending on tracked-primary versus all-checkout scope; stratified samples mixed genuine unrestricted collaborators with intentional leaf stubs and dynamic namespaces. All reviewers demonstrated that Mock(autospec=...), Mock(new=...), and Mock(new_callable=...) remain unrestricted despite being incorrectly accepted, and reproduced file-global shadowing, generated-source, patch DEFAULT/create, pytest-mocker inference, and post-construction mock_add_spec gaps. Split constructor contracts from patcher controls; constructor autospec/new/new_callable attributes now report, while exact concrete patch replacements still abstain. Added provenance-aware DEFAULT handling, create=True or dynamic-create abstention, new_callable=None handling, generated-source exclusion, top-function-local shadowing, exact pytest test/fixture mocker inference, and pre-use mock_add_spec recognition. Post-change primary-checkout calibration reports 491 warnings across 2,971 Python files; unknown replacement factories and harder subscript-rooted stub analysis remain conservative.

tasks.evidence: Three fresh independent reviews ran 30 focused tests and scanned up to 13,930 Python files. Three paths represented two unique live findings: an endpoint-mount smoke test that accepts 404 and a named crash regression whose explicit contract is only avoiding HTTP 500. Reviewers reproduced false positives from terminal-name-only HTTPStatus/framework constants and nested or non-test-class test_* functions. Ruff and Pylint have no equivalent HTTP assertion-strength rule.

tasks.evidence: Three fresh independent reviews ran 152 focused tests and scanned up to 13,930 Python files. They found 13 raw findings across eight files, including six already-suppressed bounded or transactional aggregates; only cache and task statistics were plausible analytics. Post-change calibration produced zero warnings across 2,757 consumer Python files while retaining focused synthetic coverage for newly introduced reporting scans.
